name: Cwi Bwamu
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only Berthelette & Berthelette 2001 SIL sociolinguistic survey found; no phonology/grammar of Cwi Bwamu located online.

sources.citation: Pfurtscheller, Lisa Marie. 2012. Esquisse du système tonal du bwamu laa (langue gur du Burkina Faso). Diplomarbeit, Universität Wien. xii+169 pp. doi:10.25365/thesis.19113 [sister variety Láá Láá Bwamu, bwj]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sister variety only (Boni/Bagassi = bwj), not Cwi. Three-level tone language (H, M, B, p. 49); on accent p. 95 (PDF p. 109): 'Il faut encore étudier en détail l'interaction des tons, de l'accent du bwamu laa (s'il y en a) et de l'accent français' — whether Bwamu laa has a word accent at all is left open. pp. 9-11 summarise Manessy 1961 (17 dialects, four intelligibility zones) and Berthelette 2001 (bwamu cw = Koti/Kabourou, 24,000 speakers).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page cwib1235 'Cwi Bwamu' (alt. names Bwamu Cwi, Coo, Twi) and the local Glottolog hh.bib dump
sources.note: Only two references carry [bwy]: Berthelette 2001 (overview;wordlist;socling) and Malgoubri 2020 (overview;comparative). No grammar, phonology or sketch is coded to bwy. hh.bib codes Manessy 1961's dialects to box/bmq/bwj only, Botoni 1985 (Karaba) to box, and — inconsistently — Malgoubri's Houndé/Koumbia to Bomu [bmq] while Berthelette's Koumbia/Sébédougou/Kongolikan are 'Dakwi = Bwamu-Cwi [bwy]'.

sources.citation: Yé, Dofissan Alban. 2023-2024. Une bibliographie chronologique du Buamu. Version corrigée et augmentée. Villeurbanne. 21 pp. https://archive.org/details/ye-dofissan-alban-une-bibliographie-chronologique-du-buamu-2023-2024_202409
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliography only. Every phonological description it lists is of a northern or Láá Láá parler (Bolli/Flik/Bivando 1981 Boni; Dakuyo 1985 and Dakuyo-Sanou 1989 Sanaba; Zongo-Alima 1989 Dédougou; Diarra 1994 Djibasso; Bicaba 2020 Ouakara; Pfurtscheller 2012 bwamu laa); no phonology of a Cwi or Dakwi parler (Koti, Kabourou, Bonzan, Pâ, Founzan, Koumbia, Houndé) exists in it.

sources.citation: Malgoubri, Pierre. 2020. Étude introductive sur les dialectes du bwamu: données dialectométriques, tests d'intercompréhension et dialecte de référence. In J. van der Wal, H. Smits, S. Petrollino, V. Nyst & M. Kossmann (eds.), Essays on African languages and linguistics: in honour of Maarten Mous (ASC Occasional Publications 41), 19-41. Leiden: ASCL. hdl:1887/138531
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. §2 'Données sur la langue bwamu' (p. 21) gives only 'D'un point de vue phonologique, le bwamu compte vingt consonnes et dix voyelles' plus consonant/vowel tables and class suffixes with their tones (Tableau 4, p. 22, 'ton bas / ton haut'); the rest is dialectometry over 10 localities (Bagassi, Bomborokuy, Boni, Djibasso, Houndé, Koba, Koumbia, Massala, Vy, Wakara; Pâ and Funza visited only in the pre-survey) and intercomprehension tests; p. 24 places 'le cyɛmu ou tio' in 'la zone de Koti, Oronkoa, Fara' (= Cwi). No occurrence of accent/proéminence/intensité in the chapter. Leiden's r…

sources.citation: Berthelette, John & Carol Berthelette. 2001. Sociolinguistic survey report for the Bwamu language. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2001-006. 99 pp. http://www.sil.org/silesr/2001/006/
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on phonology, tone or stress. Defines the Cwi dialect (Table 2.1.1, p. 16: Tuy west of the Mouhoun = Bonzan Bobo, Koti; Balé east of the river = Kabourou) and Dakwi (Kongolikan, Sébédougou, Koumbia); §1.9 (pp. 12-13) reviews all linguistic work (Manessy; SIL Boni phonology 1981; Yé, Botoni, Zongo mémoires; SIL Ouarkoye team 'currently preparing a paper on this dialect's phonology'); bibliography pp. 76-79 lists Grant 1997 'Tonal description of Bwamu' (unpublished ms). 230-item wordlists incl. Koti, Kabourou, Koumbia, Sébédougou, Kongolikan (appendix; phonetic text layer garbled by a c…
fr: orthography note only ('Les tons sont indiqués à l'aide de signe diacritique sur les voyelles..'), cites Berthelette 2001 and Manessy 1961; en: Ethnologue-only stub, no phonology.

sources.citation: Botoni, Charles. 1985. Synthématique en bwamu, parler de Karaba. Mémoire de maîtrise, Université de Ouagadougou
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only description of a parler inside the Cwi/Dakwi zone (Karaba, Houndé area, Tuy; 'related to Dakwi' per Berthelette 2001:24, coded [box] by Glottolog); a maîtrise mémoire normally opens with a phonological sketch.

sources.citation: Bicaba, Roland. 2020. Phonologie et morphosyntaxe du buamu (parler de Ouakara). Thèse de doctorat, Université Joseph Ki-Zerbo, Ouagadougou
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only modern full phonology of any Bwamu variety (Ouakara = Buamu [box]); a doctoral phonology is the likeliest place for an explicit statement on accent/prominence in Bwamu that could be transferred with an identity note.

sources.citation: Grant, Mary. 1997. Tonal description of Bwamu. Unpublished ms., SIL Burkina Faso (listed in Berthelette 2001:77)

sources.note: A dedicated tonal description of Bwamu (probably the Ouarkoye dialect, box) is the type of document that states whether stress plays any role beside tone.

sources.citation: Manessy, Gabriel. 1961. Le bwamu et ses dialectes. Bulletin de l'IFAN, série B (sciences humaines) 23(1/2): 119-178; reissued as Publications de la Section de Langues et Littératures 9, Faculté des Lettres et Sciences Humaines, Université de Dakar, 120 pp. + xxxvi (OCLC 10218758)

sources.note: The only multi-dialect description of Bwamu: 17 dialects surveyed incl. the southern Houndé-Kari, Yaho, Mamou and Bagassi (Pfurtscheller 2012:9-10), with grammatical sketches of nine and the standard tonal statement (three level tones, p. 127); the one place a general Bwamu remark on accent could exist that would cover the Cwi zone.
